# CANDIDATE: STRUCTURE_VETO_DIR_VS_TREND_VIX_FILTER

**Filed:** 2026-07-21  
**Filer:** chef-nemotron (free-tier autonomous R&D)  
**Type:** filter_change  
**Status:** DRAFT (NEEDS-RATIFICATION per Rule 9)

## Hypothesis

Adding a VIX>20 regime filter to the STRUCTURE_VETO_DIR_VS_TREND veto will make it more selective, only blocking trend-mismatch trades when VIX is elevated (>20). This preserves trades in low-VIX regimes where trend mismatches may be less costly or even beneficial, while maintaining protection against wrong-way trades in high-VIX environments. The goal is to improve safety (reduce losses on blocked losers) without hurting edge_capture on J's winner days, since the original veto already kept all winners and only blocked losers.

## Mechanism

The existing STRUCTURE_VETO_DIR_VS_TREND veto blocks entries when:
- Engine signal is PUT and 5m same-day trend is uptrend (P-in-uptrend)
- Engine signal is CALL and 5m same-day trend is downtrend (C-in-downtrend)

The modified veto adds a VIX condition: only block if VIX>20 AND (P-in-uptrend OR C-in-downtrend). Otherwise, no veto. VIX is measured at the same timestamp as the entry signal (using the same VIX data source as other strategies, e.g., the BEARISH_REJECTION VIX confirmation). All other logic (trend classification via `crypto.lib.market_structure.classify_trend`, entry path integration) remains unchanged.

## Confidence

6 / 10 -- Reasoning: The original veto showed clear safety benefit (blocked -$574 wrong-way losers, 0 winners) with no edge_capture impact. Adding VIX>20 filter is conservative; likely preserves most safety benefit while reducing false blocks in low-VIX regimes. However, without OOS validation, uncertainty remains about VIX regime distribution and whether low-VIX trend mismatches are truly harmless.
